newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine peso closes higher on lower dlr demand.
newsitem.headline: Philippine peso closes higher on lower dlr demand.

text.p: * Volume thins to $102 million from $159.10 million
The Philippine peso gained on Wednesday after oil firms said they would buy less dollars today and tomorrow, traders said.
The peso closed at 26.323 from 26.325, with the day's average at 26.323 from 26.324.
Dealers said the oil firms cut their dollar requirements for the day to $22.3 million from $29 million and they will buy only $19.3 million on Thursday from an earlier $29.3 million.
The Central Bank continued to intervene in the market but it did not buy as heavily as it did on Tuesday. It purchased about $6.0 million at 26.321 and $10 million at 26.323, traders said.
Traders said the peso will continue to trend upwards but it will be capped by the Central Bank.
